Comment: This is a very heavy move. Look at it this way. Black two potential weak groups at the bottom. You started out with the stone at J3 and the stone at P3. It is natural to want to save one of these stones, however it is unreasonable  to expect to save both of them. If you do try to save both of them then your opponet should get a splitting attack and it will be a disaster.   So you are going to sacrifice one stone in order to save the other. This is the essence of light play. The secret is to not make up your mind as to which stone you are going to save until you have to. You want to try to confuse your opponent so that he does not know which stone you want to save. Then, when you see how the fight is developing, you can work out what to defend and what to sacrifice.

The problem with this move is that it makes it very clear that black is trying to save the stones near the corner, and after white connects, the black stone at J3 is pretty useless. If you are going to give up a stone then you want to make it costly for your opponent to capture it.
